setup.command: Eager torchtitan Trainer, config torchtitan_recipes.graph_trainer.megatron_bridge_benchmarks.qwen3_30b_a3b_dist_moe_mxfp8_8gpu, fake process group (rank 0 of FSDP 8 x EP 8), 1 x 32768-token microbatch, local_compile off, deterministic, no activation recompute, no CUDA graphs, step 10 profiled after warmup (Kineto + ExecutionTraceObserver)

step_budget.notes: Category sums are kernel-time sums (streams overlap slightly). "other" = kernels before the forward (data/zero_grad) and after backward but before the optimizer step. Flash-attention pre/post-processing kernels (15.5 ms) are counted under attention but belong to regions. Idle time is dominated by host overhead of the capture (execution-trace observer, Python stacks, shapes), not representative of an uninstrumented step.

regions.title: Attention-backward chain: FA dq/dk/dv postprocess + RoPE bwd + QK-norm bwd + concat + MXFP8 dy quantize
regions.description: From the flash-attention fp32 dq/dk/dv accumulators to the MXFP8 (row- and column-wise) wqkv output gradient: accumulator conversion, RoPE backward, q/k RMSNorm backward, the dqkv cat and the 1x32/32x1 quantization with scale swizzles.
regions.fusion_kind: attention epilogue + pointwise + row-norm backward + quantize prologue
regions.shapes_dtypes: dq_accum [32768,32,128] fp32, dk/dv accum [4,6553600] fp32, saved xq,xk bf16, rstd -> dqkv fp8 rowwise + colwise [32768,5120] + scales
regions.bitwise_notes: The FA postprocess (scale + bf16 round) and RoPE are pointwise; the bf16 rounding points of the eager chain must be kept; RMSNorm backward reductions; amax is order-insensitive.
regions.dataflow: Each stage consumes the previous stage row by row (token, head) and the only consumer of the bf16 dqkv is the MXFP8 quantizer feeding the wqkv dgrad/wgrad GEMMs; the 32x1 column-wise blocks span 32 tokens, so the kernel tiles 32 tokens x full row.
regions.blockers: The FA postprocess kernels are inside the flash_attn library call; RMSNorm weight-grad reduction; the quantizer lives inside the MXFP8Linear backward.
regions.notes: Alternative to taking R-04 and R-17 separately; also absorbs the FA postprocess (7.6 ms) and wqkv dy quantization (6.6 ms). Member kernels: 1584; ideal from 1403.5 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: wqkv MXFP8 GEMM epilogue: QKV split + QK-norm + RoPE
regions.description: The wqkv GEMM [32768,2048]x[2048,5120] epilogue writes contiguous q/k/v directly, applying q_norm/k_norm (128-wide rows fit one output tile) and RoPE, so the [32768,5120] qkv tensor is never materialized.
regions.bitwise_notes: The GEMM output must be rounded to bf16 before the norm exactly as the eager GEMM writes it; RMSNorm reduction order over each 128-column head slice.
regions.dataflow: Each 128-column slice of the GEMM output tile is one (kv-group, slot) head; the norm needs only that slice and RoPE only its row position, so the whole chain is a per-tile epilogue.
regions.blockers: Needs a custom epilogue on the cuBLAS/nvjet MXFP8 GEMM; the RMSNorm backward needs its pre-norm input, which then must be recomputed or written as an extra output.
regions.notes: Extends the QKV split + QK-norm + RoPE region by also removing the qkv write and re-read. Member kernels: 1152; ideal from 424.4 MB external bytes and 687.2 GFLOP per instance.

regions.title: QKV split + QK-norm + RoPE forward (one kernel per layer)
regions.description: Merge of the QKV split/contiguous copies, q_norm/k_norm and RoPE: read the wqkv output once and write rotated, normalized q, k and contiguous v.
regions.bitwise_notes: Inherits the RMSNorm reduction order constraint of the QK-norm part; RoPE part is pointwise.
regions.dataflow: RoPE consumes exactly the normalized q/k rows produced by q_norm/k_norm, row by row, so the normalized values never need to reach HBM. Backward needs only rstd plus the pre-norm q/k (a view of qkv) and the cos/sin cache.
regions.blockers: Same as the two parts; RMSNorm backward would have to read its saved input from the qkv buffer.
regions.notes: Alternative to taking the QKV+QK-norm and RoPE regions separately; saves one more [32768,4608] bf16 round trip. Member kernels: 1104; ideal from 680.3 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: RoPE backward: q/k rotate-half backward chain in one pass
regions.description: Backward of CosSinRoPE for dq [32768,32,128] and dk [32768,4,128]: bf16->fp32 cast, two muls, neg, slice-backward zero-fill + copies, two adds, fp32->bf16 cast, 22 kernels per layer.
regions.fusion_kind: vertical pointwise chain + q/k sibling fusion
regions.bitwise_notes: Pointwise: grad*cos + rotate_half^T(grad*sin) in fp32 with the eager rounding order (autograd accumulates the two branches with add_).
regions.dataflow: The transpose of rotate_half is again a fixed permutation within the head dim; every output element depends on two input elements of the same row and the cache row.
regions.blockers: None structural; disabled "rope" local_compile region. Slice backward materializes zero-filled fp32 [32768,32,128] buffers twice.
regions.notes: Member kernels: 1056; ideal from 608.4 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: RoPE forward: q/k rotate-half chain in one pass
regions.description: CosSinRoPE on q [32768,32,128] and k [32768,4,128]: upcast to fp32, x*cos + rotate_half(x)*sin, cast back to bf16, plus the position bound check and cache gather, run as 18 separate kernels per layer.
regions.fusion_kind: vertical pointwise chain + q/k sibling fusion
regions.shapes_dtypes: q [32768,32,128] bf16, k [32768,4,128] bf16 -> fp32 math -> bf16; cos/sin cache [4096,256] fp32 gathered by positions [32768] int64
regions.bitwise_notes: Pure pointwise: two fp32 muls and one fp32 add per element, then a bf16 round; the fused kernel must keep the same op order and avoid FMA contraction (x*cos + y*sin evaluated as two rounded products then a rounded add).
regions.dataflow: Every op is elementwise over (token, head, dim) except rotate_half, which is a fixed permutation within the 128-wide head dim (neg + cat of halves); the cos/sin row depends only on the token position. Each element of q_out/k_out depends on two elements of the same input row and one cache row, so one pass reading q,k once and writing once is legal. q and k share the cache row (sibling fusion).
regions.blockers: None structural. This model has a "rope" local_compile region that is disabled in this capture; eager runs every op as its own kernel with fp32 intermediates (q fp32 copy, rotated copy, two products, sum).
regions.notes: Intermediates are fp32 [32768,32,128] (537 MB each), which is why eager costs ~2.1 ms/layer against an 88 us roofline. Member kernels: 864; ideal from 608.4 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Chunked cross-entropy forward + backward per chunk
regions.description: Per 4096-token chunk: fp32 upcast of the bf16 logits [4096,151936], log_softmax, nll, then immediately nll/log_softmax backward, zero-fill and bf16 downcast of the logits gradient, plus the gradient-accumulator writes.
regions.shapes_dtypes: logits [4096,151936] bf16 x 8 chunks -> loss scalar; grad logits [4096,151936] bf16; grad accumulator [32768,2048] bf16
regions.bitwise_notes: Row max/logsumexp over 151936 fp32 values must follow the cunn_SoftMax reduction order; gradient = softmax - onehot, scaled, rounded to bf16.
regions.dataflow: Backward runs right after forward on the same chunk (chunk_loss.backward()); the gradient needs only the logits row and its logsumexp, so one kernel can read logits once and write grad once. The gradient accumulator zero-fill is redundant since every slice is overwritten.
regions.blockers: Inner loss and lm_head are separate modules; the "loss" local_compile region is disabled. T3 extension: fuse with the lm_head GEMMs (linear cross-entropy).
regions.notes: ~4.4 ms per chunk against a 0.36 ms roofline. Member kernels: 115; ideal from 2489.4 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: lm_head GEMMs + chunked cross-entropy forward/backward (linear cross-entropy)
regions.description: Per 4096-token chunk, the lm_head forward GEMM, the cross-entropy forward/backward glue and the lm_head dgrad/wgrad GEMMs fused so the [4096,151936] logits and their gradient never reach HBM.
regions.bitwise_notes: Logit values come out of a GEMM; matching eager bitwise requires the same GEMM tiling/accumulation and the same logsumexp order.
regions.dataflow: The logits are consumed only by the loss and its gradient only by the two lm_head backward GEMMs; an online-softmax formulation over vocab tiles needs logits only in registers.
regions.blockers: Bitwise parity with cuBLAS GEMM outputs; lm_head is an FSDP root module with chunked backward hooks.
regions.notes: GEMMs run at the bf16 peak, so the gap equals the cross-entropy glue gap. Member kernels: 139; ideal from 1900.6 MB external bytes and 7647.2 GFLOP per instance.

regions.title: Expert weight prep per unshard: fp32->bf16 cast, copy-in, MXFP8 quantize, operand copies
regions.description: Per layer and per unshard (forward and backward), the local experts w13 [16,1536,2048] and w2 [16,2048,768] fp32 are cast to bf16, copied through the size-1 FSDP group buffer, quantized to MXFP8 with 32x32 scales by Dist-MoE, and copied into the persistent operand buffers.
regions.bitwise_notes: Cast then 32x32 amax quantization; amax is order-insensitive.
regions.dataflow: The bf16 copy exists only to feed the quantizer; the expert FSDP group has size 1 so the all-gather is a no-op copy. One kernel can read fp32 weights and write fp8 data + both scale layouts directly into the operand buffers. Expert weights do not change within a step, so the backward instance repeats identical work.
regions.blockers: FSDP2 mixed-precision cast and copy-in are generic; dist_moe.prepare_mxfp8_weight takes bf16 input and returns new tensors that are then copied. Skipping the backward re-quantization means keeping 80 MB/layer of fp8 expert weights alive across the step.
regions.notes: 96 instances = 48 forward + 48 backward unshards. Member kernels: 1152; ideal from 377.6 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Router + aux-loss backward glue (incl. deterministic gather backward)
regions.description: Backward of top-k score gather (deterministic index_put with radix sort, bounds asserts), route normalization, softmax and the load-balance loss: 62 kernels per layer over [32768,128] and [32768,8].
regions.shapes_dtypes: d topk scores [32768,8] fp32, saved scores [32768,128] fp32, ids [32768,8] int64 -> d gate logits [32768,128] fp32
regions.bitwise_notes: The gather backward is a scatter-add; with unique expert ids per token each target is written once, so a row-wise scatter is exact, but matching the eager accumulation order of the aux-loss gradient and gather gradient (add_) is required.
regions.dataflow: Every op is row-local in tokens except the aux-loss column statistics (already reduced in forward); one row-parallel kernel can scatter the 8 gradients, add the aux-loss gradient and apply the softmax backward.
regions.blockers: Deterministic mode makes index_put sort-based (~25 kernels); the bounds asserts come from index validation.
regions.notes: Member kernels: 2976; ideal from 40.9 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Router scoring + top-k bookkeeping + aux-loss forward glue
regions.description: Softmax over gate logits, round-robin expert ids, gather of top-k scores, normalization, routing-map scatter, expert counts, the batch-wise load-balance loss statistics and the padding masked_fill: 45 small kernels per layer on [32768,128] and [32768,8] tensors.
regions.shapes_dtypes: gate logits [32768,128] fp32 -> scores [32768,128] fp32, ids [32768,8] int64, topk scores [32768,8] fp32, routing map [32768,128] bool, counts [128] fp32
regions.bitwise_notes: Row softmax and column sums over 32768 tokens (expert counts, normalized-score sums) must keep the eager reduction order; the count all-reduce sits between the count and loss stages.
regions.dataflow: All ops consume the [32768,128] gate output or the [32768,8] top-k tensors; row-wise ops (softmax, gather, normalize, scatter, L1 normalize) fuse into one pass, and the column sums can be accumulated in the same pass as partial sums.
regions.blockers: The expert-count all-reduce (DP/EP) splits the region into a pre- and post-collective kernel; the deterministic column reductions over T are long and narrow (128 outputs), so a fused kernel needs a fixed-order tree reduction to stay bitwise.
regions.notes: The two column sums alone (bool->long sum and fp32 prob sums) take ~130 us/layer for 4-17 MB of input. Extension: fold the softmax into the gate GEMM epilogue (T3). Member kernels: 2160; ideal from 40.9 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Aux-loss forward + backward pair: score gradient computed in the forward pass
regions.description: The batch-wise load-balance loss forward statistics and its backward (division, norm and clamp backward over [32768,128] scores) computed together, since all backward inputs are known after the forward count all-reduce.
regions.shapes_dtypes: scores [32768,128] fp32, routing map bool -> loss scalar and dLoss/dscores [32768,128] fp32
regions.bitwise_notes: Column reductions over T and row L1 norms must keep the eager order; the backward chain (DivBackward, LinalgVectorNormBackward, ClampMinBackward) must be replicated op by op.
regions.dataflow: The injected gradient depends only on scores, routing counts (after the all-reduce), the denominator and coeff, all available at forward time; computing it once in the forward and adding it in the router backward removes ~20 backward kernels.
regions.blockers: AuxLoss.inject relies on autograd to deliver the gradient; computing it eagerly needs a custom autograd Function and stores an extra [32768,128] fp32 tensor.
regions.notes: Overlaps the router forward and router backward regions. Member kernels: 1968; ideal from 33.6 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Cross-layer: MoE combine sum + ffn residual add + next attention_norm + MXFP8 quantize
regions.description: The weighted top-k combine of layer i-1 feeding its residual add, layer i attention_norm and the wqkv-input quantization, without materializing the MoE output.
regions.shapes_dtypes: [32768,8,2048] bf16 + scores, x [32768,2048] bf16 -> x, normed bf16, fp8 + scales
regions.bitwise_notes: K-sum order, RMSNorm order.
regions.dataflow: The MoE output row is consumed only by the residual add, whose row is consumed by the next norm and quantizer: a row-parallel kernel can do all of it.
regions.blockers: Crosses the Dist-MoE library boundary and the FSDP block boundary.
regions.notes: Alternative to taking R-27 and R-15 separately. Member kernels: 239; ideal from 1546.6 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: wo dgrad GEMM epilogue computes the flash-attention backward preprocess; fold accumulator zero-fills
regions.description: The wo dgrad GEMM writes dO [32768,4096]; flash-attention backward then re-reads dO and O to compute rowsum(dO*O) per head and zero-fills its fp32 dq/dk/dv accumulators and semaphores.
regions.bitwise_notes: rowsum(dO*O) over 128 elements per head in fp32 must match the FA preprocess order, computed from the bf16-rounded dO.
regions.dataflow: Each 128-column slice of a dO output tile is one head; the epilogue has dO in registers and can load the matching O tile and reduce. The zero-fills have no inputs and can be issued by the same kernel.
regions.blockers: Requires a custom epilogue on the cuBLAS/nvjet MXFP8 GEMM and passing D into the flash-attention backward (library API change).
regions.notes: The GEMM alone runs at the measured mxfp8 peak; gap is the preprocess + zero-fills. Member kernels: 432; ideal from 832.6 MB external bytes and 549.8 GFLOP per instance.

regions.title: MoE dx combine + router-gate dgrad add + ffn_norm backward + residual-grad add + MXFP8 quantize of the wo grad
regions.description: The top-k sum of the expert input gradients, the add of the router gate input gradient, the ffn_norm RMSNorm backward, the residual gradient accumulation, and the 1x32/32x1 quantization of the result for the wo backward GEMMs.
regions.fusion_kind: reduction + gradient accumulation + RMSNorm backward + quantize
regions.shapes_dtypes: d route [32768,8,2048] bf16 + scores, d gate-input [32768,2048] bf16, saved x bf16, rstd, residual grad [32768,2048] bf16 -> grad x [32768,2048] bf16 + fp8 rowwise/colwise + scales
regions.bitwise_notes: K-sum order, autograd accumulation order (experts first, then gate), RMSNorm backward reductions; amax is order-insensitive.
regions.dataflow: The ffn_norm output gradient is the sum of two producers (experts and gate) and is consumed only by the norm backward; the norm backward output plus the residual gradient is the grad of the attention residual stream, consumed by the wo backward (quantized) and passed down the residual.
regions.blockers: The expert dx sum is inside the Dist-MoE backward custom op; autograd performs the gradient accumulation as separate add_ kernels; ffn_norm weight-grad column reduction.
regions.notes: Member kernels: 384; ideal from 1750.2 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Dist-MoE forward combine: weighted top-k sum
regions.description: Reduces the expert outputs scattered into [32768,8,2048] bf16 by the router scores into the MoE output [32768,2048].
regions.bitwise_notes: Sum over K=8 in fixed order with fp32 accumulation.
regions.dataflow: Single memory-bound reduction; runs at 54% of HBM roofline.
regions.blockers: The [T,K,D] buffer is written by remote ranks' combine GEMM epilogues (symmetric memory); folding the K-sum into those epilogues would need cross-rank atomics (non-deterministic).
regions.notes: The zero-fill that precedes it in this capture is a fake-PG artifact (see no_opportunity). Member kernels: 48; ideal from 1209.0 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: FSDP reduce-scatter glue: chunk_cat, size-1 group copy, fp32 gradient cast
regions.description: Per layer: chunk_cat of the expert gradients and attention-group gradients into reduce-scatter buffers, the size-1 expert group copy, and casts of the reduced shards to fp32.
regions.shapes_dtypes: expert grads [16,2,768,2048]+[16,2048,768] bf16 -> fp32 shard; attention grads -> bf16 [8,2392608] -> fp32 shard
regions.bitwise_notes: Copies and casts only.
regions.dataflow: For the size-1 expert group, chunk_cat -> copy -> cast is one bf16->fp32 cast of the gradients; for the attention group the post-reduce cast can be folded into the reduce-scatter output copy.
regions.blockers: FSDP2 generic reduce-scatter path; T3 extension: wgrad GEMMs writing directly into the reduce-scatter buffer.
regions.notes: Member kernels: 336; ideal from 543.9 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: q_norm/k_norm backward + dqkv concat
regions.description: RMSNorm backward for q and k heads (with their weight-grad row reductions) and the SplitWithSizes backward cat that reassembles dq/dk/dv into the [32768,5120] wqkv gradient.
regions.shapes_dtypes: dq,dk bf16 + saved xq,xk bf16 + rstd fp32, dv [32768,4,128] bf16 -> dqkv [32768,4,10,128] bf16; dweight [128] fp32
regions.bitwise_notes: RMSNorm backward row reduction and the [128] weight-grad column reduction order.
regions.dataflow: q_norm/k_norm backward outputs are consumed only by the cat; writing directly into the strided dqkv slots removes the cat.
regions.blockers: Weight-grad column reduction across 32768x32 rows needs a second pass or a fixed-order cross-CTA reduction.
regions.notes: Member kernels: 240; ideal from 977.8 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: FSDP attention-group unshard glue (forward and backward re-unshard)
regions.description: Per layer and per unshard: fp32->bf16 casts of the wqkv/wo shards, copy-in to the all-gather buffer, copy-out split, MXFP8 32x32 weight quantization of wqkv [5120,2048] and wo [2048,4096] with swizzled scales, and copies of the fp8 data/scales into FSDP-managed operand buffers.
regions.shapes_dtypes: fp32 shards [640,2048], [256,4096] + small params -> bf16 [8,2392608] all-gather buffer -> fp8 wqkv [5120,2048], wo [2048,4096] + 32x32 e8m0 scales
regions.bitwise_notes: Cast and quantize are exact functions of the inputs; 32x32 amax is order-insensitive.
regions.dataflow: Pre-collective: the cast output is only copied into the all-gather input buffer (cast directly into it). Post-collective: the gathered bf16 weights are only quantized and the quantized operands are copied into persistent buffers (quantize directly into them; skip the bf16 unsharded copy-out for wqkv/wo).
regions.blockers: FSDP2 owns copy-in/copy-out and the all-gather boundary; the operand copy exists because _build_operands refills FSDP-managed buffers. The backward instance re-does the forward work because blocks reshard after forward (keeping fp8 operands costs ~20 MB/layer).
regions.notes: 96 instances = 48 forward + 48 backward unshards. Member kernels: 1344; ideal from 72.1 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: QKV split/contiguous copies + q_norm + k_norm forward
regions.description: The wqkv output [32768,5120] is split into q/k/v and copied contiguous (3 copies), then q_norm and k_norm (RMSNorm over head_dim 128) run as separate kernels.
regions.bitwise_notes: RMSNorm reduces over 128 elements per (token, head); the fused kernel must reproduce the quack RMSNorm reduction order.
regions.dataflow: q_norm/k_norm read only the split views of qkv; v needs only a strided copy. A single kernel can read each qkv row once and emit normalized q, k and contiguous v. q_norm and k_norm are siblings over the same input row.
regions.blockers: The contiguous copies exist for vLLM KV-cache layout compatibility (comment in QKVLinear.forward); a fused kernel must still produce contiguous outputs. The RMSNorm backward saves its input, which would become a view of qkv.
regions.notes: Member kernels: 240; ideal from 675.8 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Dist-MoE forward routing-plan metadata kernels
regions.description: Per layer, ten small Dist-MoE kernels build the expert-parallel dispatch plan from the gathered top-k expert ids (routing split, prefix, combine, metadata gather, block-scaled plan, two GEMM scheduler preparations, small cat/copies).
regions.shapes_dtypes: expert ids [8,32768,8] int64 (all EP ranks) -> gather/scatter index tables per local expert, token counts
regions.bitwise_notes: Slot assignment uses prefix sums over tokens; outputs are integer indices, so bitwise equality requires the same slot order (order-sensitive data movement).
regions.dataflow: Each stage consumes the previous stage's counts/offsets; routing split -> prefix -> combine is a classic histogram/scan/scatter that fits one persistent kernel with grid-wide sync or a decoupled look-back scan.
regions.blockers: Inside the dist_moe library; the stages are separated by cross-rank metadata exchange in the real job (gathered ids), and the routing split kernel itself is 55 us of the 87 us.
regions.notes: With round-robin routing the plan is identical every layer and every step; caching it would remove the region (configuration-specific). Member kernels: 480; ideal from 23.1 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Dist-MoE backward: broadcast and scale dy into [T,K,D] with score gradients
regions.description: Broadcasts the MoE output gradient to every routed slot scaled by its router score and computes the score gradient as a dot product with the saved route outputs.
regions.bitwise_notes: Score gradient is a 2048-long dot product per (token, k); order must match.
regions.dataflow: Single kernel already; 80% of roofline. T3 extension: apply the per-row score in the dgrad dispatch GEMM prologue so the 1.07 GB scaled-dy buffer is never written.
regions.blockers: The dgrad dispatch GEMM reads the scaled gradient through remote symmetric memory; scaling in its prologue is a Dist-MoE kernel change.
regions.notes: Member kernels: 48; ideal from 2283.8 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: HiMidLo gate weight gradient: three per-piece GEMMs + adds -> one GEMM
regions.description: The router gate weight gradient is computed as three [128,32768]x[32768,2048] split-K GEMMs (one per bf16 piece) with split-K reduce kernels, then two fp32 adds and a bf16 cast.
regions.fusion_kind: horizontal GEMM fusion with epilogue accumulation
regions.bitwise_notes: Accumulating the three pieces inside one GEMM changes the fp32 rounding order relative to three separately rounded GEMM results plus two adds.
regions.dataflow: All three GEMMs read the same x; one GEMM over K=3x32768 (or one kernel with three accumulators) reads x once.
regions.blockers: Bitwise equality with the eager per-piece rounding; cuBLAS split-K heuristics.
regions.notes: Overlaps the HiMidLo glue region on the adds and cast. Member kernels: 432; ideal from 159.9 MB external bytes and 51.5 GFLOP per instance.

regions.title: Forward-backward: column-wise MXFP8 of the wqkv/wo inputs produced in the forward
regions.description: The wqkv and wo backward re-read the saved bf16 inputs (normed x [32768,2048], attention output [32768,4096]) to quantize them column-wise (32x1) for the weight-gradient GEMMs.
regions.shapes_dtypes: saved x [32768,2048] bf16 -> fp8 colwise + scales; saved O [32768,4096] bf16 -> fp8 colwise + scales
regions.bitwise_notes: 32x1 amax is order-insensitive; requires the forward producers (attention_norm, attention epilogue) to emit the column-wise blocks.
regions.dataflow: The column-wise quantization depends only on forward values; the forward norm (R-27) and attention epilogue (R-28) already hold these tiles.
regions.blockers: The capture saves inputs in bf16 (96 bf16, 0 mxfp8 saved formats); for the attention output the bf16 copy must stay for the flash-attention backward, so this adds 138 MB/layer of saved fp8.
regions.notes: Ideal = incremental forward writes of the column-wise operands. Member kernels: 192; ideal from 207.6 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: attention_norm backward + residual-grad add
regions.description: RMSNorm backward of attention_norm and the autograd add_ that accumulates it into the residual-stream gradient.
regions.fusion_kind: RMSNorm backward with fused residual-grad accumulation
regions.shapes_dtypes: d normed [32768,2048] bf16, saved x bf16, rstd fp32, residual grad [32768,2048] bf16 -> grad x [32768,2048] bf16
regions.bitwise_notes: RMSNorm backward row reduction; the add of the residual grad happens after the bf16 rounding of the norm grad.
regions.dataflow: The norm backward output is consumed only by the accumulation add_.
regions.blockers: Autograd accumulation is a separate kernel; T3 extension into the wqkv dgrad GEMM epilogue would also remove the d normed round trip.
regions.notes: Member kernels: 144; ideal from 537.0 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Attention residual add + ffn_norm + Dist-MoE dispatch copy
regions.description: x + attn_out, the ffn_norm RMSNorm, and the Dist-MoE kernel that copies the normalized tokens (and routing ids/scores) into the expert-parallel dispatch buffer.
regions.fusion_kind: residual add + RMSNorm writing into the dispatch buffer
regions.shapes_dtypes: x, attn_out [32768,2048] bf16 -> x [32768,2048] bf16, normed [32768,2048] bf16 in the symmetric dispatch buffer; ids/scores [32768,8]
regions.bitwise_notes: RMSNorm row reduction order.
regions.dataflow: The normed tokens are consumed by the router gate GEMM and copied verbatim into the dispatch buffer; writing them once directly into the dispatch buffer removes one [32768,2048] read+write.
regions.blockers: Dist-MoE owns the symmetric-memory dispatch buffer and its conditional (activation-slot) placement; the router gate GEMM and saved activations would read from that buffer.
regions.notes: Member kernels: 144; ideal from 543.2 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: HiMidLo router-gate backward glue: bf16 piece split, concats, weight-grad adds
regions.description: Splits the fp32 gate gradient [32768,128] into three bf16 pieces (casts, shift, subtracts), concatenates pieces and weight copies for the stacked GEMMs, adds the per-piece weight gradients and casts to bf16.
regions.bitwise_notes: Exact bit manipulations (bf16 round, shift-upcast, subtract) and copies.
regions.dataflow: All pieces derive elementwise from the fp32 gradient; writing them directly in the stacked layout removes the cats.
regions.blockers: Disabled "fp32_to_bf16_split" local_compile region. T3 extension: split in registers inside the GEMM prologue (noted as TODO in the source).
regions.notes: Member kernels: 672; ideal from 47.7 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Cross-layer: ffn residual add + next attention_norm + MXFP8 quantize of the wqkv input
regions.description: Layer i-1's trailing residual add (x + ffn_out), layer i's attention_norm RMSNorm and the 1x32 MXFP8 quantization (+ scale swizzle) of the normalized activations for the wqkv GEMM.
regions.bitwise_notes: RMSNorm row reduction over 2048 must match the quack kernel order; the 1x32 amax is order-insensitive (max).
regions.dataflow: The add output is the residual stream x consumed row-wise by the norm; the norm output row is consumed only by the MXFP8 quantizer (and saved in bf16 for the wgrad). One row-parallel kernel can do add -> rmsnorm -> amax/scale/cast per 32-element block -> swizzled scale write.
regions.blockers: Crosses the FSDP block boundary (the add is in block i-1, the norm in block i; FSDP pre-forward hooks of block i run in between). The quantizer is inside the MXFP8Linear autograd Function, so the norm output must be passed in pre-quantized. Layer 0 has no preceding add.
regions.notes: 47 adds + 48 norms + 48 quantize + 48 swizzle kernels. Member kernels: 191; ideal from 606.1 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: MXFP8 quantize of the attention output in the flash-attention forward epilogue
regions.description: The wo input (attention output [32768,4096] bf16) is quantized to MXFP8 1x32 plus scale swizzle by two separate kernels right after flash attention writes it.
regions.bitwise_notes: The quantization itself is exact given O; but it requires changes inside the flash-attention kernel epilogue (bf16 O must still be written for the attention backward).
regions.dataflow: Each output tile of the attention kernel is a complete set of 32-element blocks along head_dim (128), so the per-block amax/scale can be computed in the epilogue from registers.
regions.blockers: Flash attention is a library kernel (CuTe DSL flash_attn); the quantized output must be handed to the MXFP8Linear Function. Ideal counts only the extra fp8+scale bytes written by the epilogue (attention kernel time is excluded since document lengths are unknown).
regions.notes: Ideal = incremental bytes only (138 MB/layer), not the full attention. Member kernels: 96; ideal from 138.4 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Router gate dgrad GEMM accumulates into the expert input gradient (beta=1 epilogue)
regions.description: The HiMidLo gate input-gradient GEMM [32768,384]x[384,2048] writes a fresh bf16 [32768,2048] tensor that autograd then adds into the routed-experts input gradient with a separate add_.
regions.shapes_dtypes: pieces [32768,384] bf16 x stacked W [384,2048] bf16 -> += d ffn_norm-output [32768,2048] bf16
regions.bitwise_notes: Eager rounds the GEMM result to bf16, then adds in fp32 and rounds again; the epilogue must round the accumulator to bf16 before adding C to stay bitwise.
regions.dataflow: The GEMM output is consumed only by the accumulation into the gradient buffer that the expert backward already produced.
regions.blockers: Autograd owns gradient accumulation; the Function would need the existing gradient buffer as an in/out operand (the code already does this for weight gradients).
regions.notes: Overlaps R-14 on the add_ kernel. Member kernels: 96; ideal from 295.2 MB external bytes and 51.5 GFLOP per instance.

regions.title: wo MXFP8 GEMM epilogue adds the attention residual
regions.description: The wo projection GEMM [32768,4096]x[4096,2048] writes attn_out, then a separate kernel computes x + attn_out.
regions.bitwise_notes: The epilogue must round the GEMM accumulator to bf16 (attn_out) before the bf16 residual add, as eager does.
regions.dataflow: attn_out is consumed only by the residual add (it is not saved for backward); the add is elementwise on the GEMM output tile.
regions.blockers: Custom epilogue on the MXFP8 GEMM inside the MXFP8Linear Function; the residual lives outside the attention module. The following ffn_norm needs whole 2048-wide rows, which a tile epilogue does not see.
regions.notes: Overlaps R-25 on the residual add. Member kernels: 96; ideal from 415.3 MB external bytes and 549.8 GFLOP per instance.

regions.title: Dist-MoE backward plan/metadata kernels
regions.description: Backward plan construction, activation-to-dispatch copy and four GEMM scheduler preparation kernels per layer.
regions.fusion_kind: metadata pipeline fusion / reuse of forward plan
regions.bitwise_notes: Integer index tables; same slot order required.
regions.dataflow: The backward plan is a function of the forward routing; it could be produced together with the forward plan.
regions.blockers: Inside the dist_moe library.
regions.notes: Member kernels: 384; ideal from 10.5 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Root FSDP groups (tok_embeddings, norm+lm_head): unshard and reduce-scatter glue
regions.description: Cast/copy-in, copy-out of the all-gathered [151936,2048] embedding and lm_head weights (lm_head re-gathered for the decoder backward), chunk_cat into the reduce-scatter buffer and fp32 cast of the reduced shard.
regions.bitwise_notes: Pure copies and casts.
regions.dataflow: For single-parameter groups the dim-0 all-gather output already has the parameter layout, so copy-out and chunk_cat are layout no-ops; casts fold into the copy-in and the post-reduce copy.
regions.blockers: FSDP2 generic buffer management; norm weight is packed with lm_head so that group needs a strided copy.
regions.notes: Ideal assumes a copy-out is still needed for the packed (norm, lm_head) group only. Member kernels: 21; ideal from 1089.1 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Embedding backward (deterministic sort-based scatter-add)
regions.description: Gradient of tok_embeddings: zero-fill of [151936,2048], radix sort of token ids, segment reduction and scatter.
regions.bitwise_notes: Segment sums over duplicate token ids must follow the sorted order.
regions.dataflow: Zero-fill and scatter of the same buffer can be one kernel; sort + segment reduce is the deterministic contract.
regions.blockers: Single instance; library implementation.
regions.notes: Member kernels: 21; ideal from 756.8 MB external bytes per instance.

regions.title: Last-layer residual add + final norm forward, final norm backward
regions.description: Layer 47 trailing residual add fused with the final RMSNorm, and the final RMSNorm backward with its weight-grad reduction.
regions.bitwise_notes: Row reductions of RMSNorm forward/backward and the column reduction for the weight gradient.
regions.dataflow: Same as the per-layer residual+norm pattern; single instance.
regions.blockers: Final norm is a separate FSDP root module; negligible size.
regions.notes: Member kernels: 4; ideal from 1073.7 MB external bytes per instance.
